articles.title: ‘People should not feel guilty’: weekend lie-in may be good for you, experts say
articles.summary: Previous advice stressed risks of sleeping in but about 90 minutes extra could prevent high blood pressure. For years, experts have stressed the risks of lie-ins, warning that catching up on missed sleep at the weekend can disrupt the body’s internal clock and trigger adverse health effects.
body: Now analysis has produced a heartening caveat to that advice: if you do not overdo it, weekend lie-ins may be good for you, with an ideal benchmark of 1hr 27min extra in bed to protect against high blood pressure.

Most experts still agree that setting a routine bedtime and wake-up time is key to maintaining good health. But a new study shows a modest amount of catch-up sleep – one to two hours extra – after a long week is associated with a lower prevalence of high blood pressure.
Globally, more than 1.3 billion people have hypertension. They face a much higher risk of heart attack, stroke, kidney disease and early death.

While other ways to avoid high blood pressure remain crucial – such as staying active, maintaining a healthy weight and eating well – the study suggests people should no longer feel guilty about getting up late at the weekend, experts said.

articles.title: The lost art of guilt-free relaxation on Sundays | Letters
articles.summary: Readers respond to an article about le dimanche français, the French Sunday, being the secret to happiness. What Polly Hudson describes as le dimanche français is almost a description of the very British Sundays of my youth ( Is a French Sunday the secret to a healthier, happier life?, 23 August ).
body: We enjoyed a good book (not a heavy one), an afternoon film on TV, board games, cards, or a gentle stroll for the pleasure of it rather than as part of a keep-fit regime. And let us not forget time to peruse the Sunday newspapers. Children got bored and learned how to entertain themselves, a skill today’s hard-pressed parents underestimate as they struggle to ensure Sundays are packed with activities.

There were no home computers and shops were closed, as were cinemas, swimming pools, theme parks and even pubs in certain parts of the country. This was occasionally frustrating, but more usually an advantage, removing the temptation to feel like one ought to be doing something, thus enhancing a guilt-free mindset. It was wonderful.
Importantly, it was the same day of the week for everyone. That made a difference. The whole atmosphere was quieter.
So what changed? My impression is that the whole rhythm of the week changed with Sunday trading. I’m not sure a younger generation would even recognise the phrase. Oh, were it possible to go back.

articles.title: I have diarrhea. What should I do?
articles.summary: The discussion about diarrhea has increased lately, especially with the rise of cyclosporiasis. Although unpleasant, it is manageable and can be treated at home. In the US, people are discussing diarrhea more than usual.
body: Some causes, such as cyclospora infection, benefit from antibiotic treatment. But most episodes of diarrhea go away by themselves and don’t require treatment apart from staying hydrated, says Benjamin Levy, a gastroenterologist at the University of Chicago.
Although it’s unpleasant, it’s usually manageable. Here’s how to know when to seek care, and how to take care of yourself at home.
The majority of diarrhea episodes go away by themselves after three or four days, says Levy.

However, if you have diarrhea that has lasted longer than a week or is accompanied by fever or other concerning symptoms, seek care. These include a fever of 101F or higher, blood or mucus in your stool, severe abdominal pain, vomiting for more than two to three days, or feeling like you need to poop but not actually producing anything when you go to the bathroom.

articles.title: The kindness of strangers: My car had been towed and my kids had no shoes, then a man made a wonderful offer
articles.summary: Can you help me?, I asked. I think my car’s been towed away, and my children don’t have any shoes. One of the first things we did after moving from the UK to Vancouver was buy a car. Unfortunately, I didn’t acquaint myself with the new road rules quite as quickly.
body: Which is to say, I didn’t know you aren’t allowed to park on busy streets after 3pm in Vancouver. Unaware and in a carefree summer mood, I parked outside an ice-cream shop and took my barefoot children in for a treat. We emerged a short time later, sticky and splattered in drops of raspberry, mint and chocolate, and found my car wasn’t there.

We were so fresh to Canada that we were still staying in a hotel. So I headed out on foot, one kid under each arm, towards our accommodation. When I reached the concierge desk of the valet parking place out the front, I frantically turned to the nicely dressed man standing there and launched into explaining our situation.
“Hi, can you help me? I think my car’s been towed away, and my children don’t have any shoes. I’m sorry about the ice-cream, but can you help me get to wherever the towing place is?”

He answered yes, of course, he was happy to help. After I badgered him about whether he’d have car seats for the kids, he said that we best get going, as he had to be back by 5pm. When I asked why, he replied, “Well, I’ve got a flight to catch.”

articles.title: Claudia Sulewski and Finneas Are Married! Inside the Bride’s Final Fitting at Oscar de la Renta
articles.summary: On Saturday, the beauty founder and musician tied the knot in Santa Barbara—but only after the bride invited Vogue along to the final fitting of her four Oscar de la Renta wedding looks in Beverly Hills.
body: Congratulations are in order for Finneas and Claudia Sulewski: the couple married on Saturday, August 29, in Montecito, surrounded by family and friends. Just under two weeks before, Vogue followed along as the actor and beauty founder bride headed to the Oscar de la Renta boutique in Beverly Hills for the final fitting of her four wedding weekend looks, all custom-made by the legendary American fashion house. “I’m so excited,” Claudia says, inviting us through the door. “Let’s go!”

The morning began with Claudia greeting her mom, Beata Sulewska, and her now-mother-in-law, Maggie Baird, and outlining the run of show: trying on her rehearsal dinner dress, ceremony dress, first dance and reception dress, and the after-party dress. The one she’s most excited about? The main ceremony dress, of course. “Every fitting thus far has sort of been an alteration, so I’m really excited to try on the final version,” Claudia adds.
Claudia in her after-party dress, accompanied by (from left to right) friends Dru MacDonald and Rebecca Black, her mother Beata Krupinska-Sulewski, and her now-mother-in-law Maggie Baird.

articles.title: 16 Idyllic Hotels in the Catskills, Where Design Meets the Upstate Wild
articles.summary: Whether you’re a city dweller craving fresh air or a local looking for a refined weekend retreat, these properties combine modern comfort with an easy sense of place.
body: I’ve been going to the Catskills for as long as I can remember, and I still adore the feeling when the drive north begins to feel less like a commute and more like a true escape from the city. As a native New Yorker, I’ve spent years getting to know this upstate mountain region in every season: summer afternoons bouncing between swimming holes and farm stands, brilliant fall drives beneath canopies of red and gold, spring weekends when the woods suddenly turn electric green, and winter stays where a fire and a good dinner can easily constitute the entire itinerary.
At Blue Fox Motel, the refreshed midcentury cabins will make you swoon.

articles.title: Seeking Texas's Sartorial Soul in Forth Worth, an Apex of Cowboy Culture and Craft
articles.summary: Christine Lennon does a deep dive into what has become an epicenter of haute-rodeo lifestyle and a prime destination for bespoke high-end westernwear.
body: As I look around the coliseum, there is ample evidence confirming my belief that Texans don't do subtle and they don't want to blend in. Texans have always seemed to relish their otherness, maybe even more so now that, in our age of globalization, so much sameness has infiltrated most American and international cities. I flew to Fort Worth from my hometown of Los Angeles with the hope of seeing some of this bold individualism firsthand and to check out how this North Central Texas city has grown into the epicenter of the haute-rodeo lifestyle and the premier destination for custom high-end Westernwear.

“If you remember seeing one of these as a kid, then we can guess how old you are,” boot fitter Jeff Stevens says with a wink, walking toward me with a vintage metal Brannock device to measure my feet. I'm at Rod Patrick Bootmakers, a 51-year-old local brand in Arlington Heights, not far from my hotel in the Cultural District. It's known for carrying sizes 4 through 17 with a whopping 13 different widths. The walls are lined with photos of rodeo-star customers, and a classic from the Charlie Daniels Band that I haven't heard since the '80s plays through the speakers.

articles.title: All the Celebrity Sightings at the 2026 U.S. Open
articles.summary: The annual tennis event has turned into an opportunity for stars to step out in their best courtside looks.
body: The 2026 U.S. Open has officially kicked off in Queens, New York City. Just a few days into the annual tournament, we’ve already seen some of the sport’s biggest tennis pros hit the court in style—including world-class players like Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, and Roger Federer.

While much of the excitement will be happening on the court, the event is about more than just the scores: In recent years, the U.S. Open has become a high-profile opportunity for stars to step out in their best courside looks (and flaunt their lucrative brand deals to boot). It’s as much a fashion event as it is a sporting one—just take the latest fashion-forward sightings in the fan stands.

Vogue September cover stars Kaia Gerber and Homer Gere, for one, hit the first week of the U.S. Open in sophisticated outfits. Gerber looked chic in her form-fitting little black dress, while Gere went classic in his blazer, jeans, and crisp white collared shirt. There were even loads of designer sightings amongst the crowd, too: Both Vera Wang and Tory Burch made cameos.
